# MMA structure

The MMA webpage is created in [quarto markdown](https://quarto.org/). The quarto
markdown [documentation](https://quarto-tdg.org/) is extensive. You should view
the [Websites](https://quarto-tdg.org/websites) section. Quarto markdown (qmd)
mostly matches Markdown syntax, which is very intuitive and easy to write.
Quarto's [markdown
basics](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html) will help you
get started with markdown if you are new to it. Most of the LaTeX that you are
used to works here. I edit my qmd files in VS Code. 

This webpage is split into two main trees, both of which link to the other side.

- **Application topic**: These form a tree: Chemistry > Reaction equations >
Kinetics.
- **Math topic**: an area of math, e.g. Logarithms or Differential equations.

The webpage is created through a series of .qmd files in a file directory.
Several terms will be used in this document. They are defined below. 


## Terms {#sec-terms}
- **Hub**: a page that introduces a topic and lists relevant pages. 
  A hub has a short background and an automatic list (see *listing*) of
  connected pages (e.g., sub applications or associated mathematics). A hub has
  no or worksheets of its own. Those are in **conections**. Each application
  topic and each math topic has a hub, e.g. the Chemical Kinetics hub or the
  Logarithms hub. Hubs should not need much editing, since they are
  automatically built with listings (see below). 
- **Connection**: a page about one application topic used with one math
  topic, e.g. *Chemical Kinetics & Differential equations*. This is the core of
  MMA. Connection pages are the main page users will access, usually through a
  "filter chip".  A connection page has, in order: 
  - **Background**: an explanation of the application and how the math
   applies, written for instructors, but easy for instructors to copy if they
   want to share background information with students. The background should be
   written in three ways so instructors can easily share the level of detail they
   want to share with students. 
     - *Minimum*: a paragraph you could put on a homework assignment or worksheet. 
     - *Medium*: a longer explanation, e.g., something that could be discussed
       verbally in class in 5 minutes. 
     - *Extended*: a deep dive, with references. This is mostly used for
       instructors or those wishing to learn more about the topic. 
  - **Prerequisite**: material students should know before starting a
    connection or resource. Link it to the page that covers it, if there is one.
  - **Learning outcome**: what students can do after a connection or
    resource, written with a measurable verb ("Convert...", "Interpret...",
    not "Understand..."). See [REVISED Bloom's Taxonomy Action Verbs](https://www.educ.msstate.edu/sites/www.educ.msstate.edu/files/2026-03/blooms_taxonomy_action_verbs.pdf)
    - TODO: should these be here, or in the resources, or both? It would be nice to have these on the page as clickable resources. Maybe we make a listing for these?
- **Resource**: something instructors can use in class that belongs to one
  connection: a lesson, worksheet, problem set, etc. Each resource is its own
  page, kept in the `resources/` folder of its connection.
  - **Learning outcome**: what students can do after a connection or
    resource, written with a measurable verb ("Convert...", "Interpret...",
    not "Understand..."). See [REVISED Bloom's Taxonomy Action Verbs](https://www.educ.msstate.edu/sites/www.educ.msstate.edu/files/2026-03/blooms_taxonomy_action_verbs.pdf)
- **Tag**: a label in a page's `categories:` list (see [Page YAML headers](#sec-YAML)), e.g.
  `categories: [Kinetics, Logarithms]`. Tags are how a page shows up on
  math topic hubs (using *listings*, see below). A tag must match the hub's
  title exactly: "Logarithm" will not match "Logarithms".
- **Listing**: an automatic list of pages, built by Quarto every time the
  site is rendered. Hubs use
  [listings](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings-custom.html), so
  they are automatically updated when a new connection is added. 
  
## Webpage structure 
Every viewable page (Hub, Connection, or Resource) is the `index.qmd` file
inside its own folder, so the folders below match the pages of the website. For
example:

- **Homepage**: `index.qmd`
  - **Application topics**: `applications/`
    - **Chemistry** (hub): `chemistry/`
      - **Reaction equations** (hub): `reaction-equations/`
        - **Chemical Kinetics** (hub): `kinetics/`
          - **Chemical Kinetics & Differential equations** (connection): `odes/`
            - Resources (lessons, worksheets, ...): `resources/*.qmd`
          - **Chemical Kinetics & Logarithms** (connection): `logarithms/`
            - Resources (lessons, worksheets, ...): `resources/*.qmd`
        - **Stoichiometry** (hub): `stoichiometry/`
      - **Titration** (hub): `titration/`
  - **Math topics**: `math/`
    - **Logarithms** (hub): `logarithms/`
    - **Differential equations** (hub): `differential-equations/`


## Site-wide files
These files apply to the whole site, defining site structure and style. Most
contributors won't need to edit them, but you may want to experiment with
changes on your own GitHub branch.

**Files and folders whose names start with `_` are not turned into pages and may not be visible to you when you pull from GitHub.**

- `_quarto.yml`: the site's settings: the site title, the navigation bar
  at the top of every page, the theme, and defaults for every page (for
  example, a table of contents on every page `toc: true`). A setting in a page's
  own YAML header overrides the default here for that page. Changes here affect
  every page; edits must be approved by the site administrator (Jeremy).
- `styles.css`: custom styling (colors, spacing, fonts) added on top of
  the theme. This is not in use right now, but may be something you want to edit
  if you want specific styles. 
- `_templates/`: starter files for new hub, connection and resource pages.
- `_site/`: the built website, created by `quarto render`. Don't edit
  anything here; it is replaced every time the site is built.
- `.quarto/`: Quarto's internal working files, created automatically when
  the site is rendered. **Don't edit it. It is safe to delete because
  Quarto rebuilds it with each rendering.** 
- `.gitignore`: a file telling GitHub which files/folders to ignore when pushing
  to the repository. 


## How pages work
Each page is a `.qmd` file consisting of a
[YAML](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YAML) header (delineated with `---`),
containing the page settings, followed by the page's text. The page text is
written in markdown and should be relatively straightforward. The header anatomy
is described below. 

#### Page YAML headers {#sec-YAML}
Each page begins with a YAML header, enclosed with `---`. Here is an example,
from the [Chemical Kinetics page](./applications/chemistry/reaction-equations/kinetics/index.qmd).

```yaml
---
title: "Chemical Kinetics"
description: "Modeling reactant concentrations as functions time."
categories: [Chemistry, Reaction equations]
listing:
  id: connections
  contents: "./*/index.qmd"
  type: table
  fields: [title, description, categories]
  sort: title
---
```


The following table describes what different header settings do, how to use
them, and when you might want to use them. 

- `title`: The page's heading and the name in the browser tab. When this page
  appears in a list on another page (e.g., through a listing), this is the link
  text.
- `description`: A summary shown under the title. When this page appears in a
  list on another page, this is the text beside the link. Ideally this should be
  one sentence and certainly no more than two sentences.
- `categories`: A list of the page's tags. They appear as small labels under the
  page title. Categories are used for searching and organization. See [quarto's description](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings). 
- `listing`: This creates a "listing" (see @sec-terms), an automatic list of other
  pages on the site matching specifications defined below. This needs to be
  edited to define the contents and look of the listing. **Multiple listings can exist on one page, creating two searchable tables.**
  - `id: connections`: The list's name (`connections`). It tells Quarto where to
    put the list on the page (see #page-body). This is arbitrary, you decide it.
  - `contents`: Which pages to list. `./*/index.qmd` means "all files named
    `index.qmd` in the next-level of subdirectories." Each connection page will
    displayed in its own row. 
  - `type: table`: Show the list as a table. [Other options](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings#listing-types): `default` (a list
    with summaries) and `grid` (cards).
  - `fields: [title, description, categories]`: The columns of the listing
    table. These come from the listed page's own header. These are searchable in
    the listing.  
  - `sort: title`:  Order the rows alphabetically by title. See [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings#listing-types) for other options.
- `toc: false`: `toc` means "table of contents". By default, `toc` is `true` which creates a table of contents in the rigth margin. For short pages, you may have `toc: false`.

#### Page body 
The page body depends on whether the page is a Hub, Connection, or Resource.  

#### Page listing
The listing, defined in the header, should be placed at the bottom of the page.
To show it on the webpage, put an empty block with the list's `id` in the page
text, where the list should appear:

```markdown
## Math connections

::: {#connections}
:::
```
::: {.callout-note}
`:::` creates a "fence" in qmd. Fences are used to create HTML `<div>` or
`<span>` elements. See the [pandoc user
guide](https://pandoc.org/demo/example33/8.18-divs-and-spans.html) for more. You will often see / use them to create special elements.
:::

Without this block, Quarto automatically puts the list at the end of the page
without a header. 


## Templates
You can use existing pages as templates, or find templates in `./_templates/`.
